title: JSP-000925: strict derivative-root gaps with selector existence, uniqueness and verified Lean proofs
body:
> **2026-09-19 self-check update:** the exact listed proof versions passed the complete bundled `lean-verify` workflow. See the pinned report and fresh execution evidence below. Mathematical review and official acceptance remain pending. The self-check is optional evidence under the current rules. Related claim: [#1585](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/issues/1585).

## Submission type

- [ ] Mathematical solver information
- [x] Lean proof or formalization author information

## Submission status and current guidance

This updates [existing PR #342](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/pull/342) in place under the [submission guidance](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/0e93024c553ff533692f1b10af5fbe53050ea2b6/CONTRIBUTING.md) reviewed on 2026-09-20. Its diff changes only the relevant catalog entry; the Lean source and build materials are hosted in the external repository pinned below. This is not a new source-code submission or a claim to a new priority date. Related existing claim: [#1585](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/issues/1585).

Mathematical review must pass before Lean acceptance. Solver registration or an award claim by the mathematical solver is not a prerequisite for Lean verification or Lean candidate registration. The two contribution types can be registered independently.

The [`lean-verify` self-check is optional](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/0e93024c553ff533692f1b10af5fbe53050ea2b6/docs/verification.md#recommended-lean-pre-submission-check). The dated reports below remain evidence of the specific checks actually run, using their recorded historical versions. Their older administrative descriptions are superseded by the current guidance linked here; their proof results, dates and limitations are not re-dated or extended to untested versions.

## Problem and proposed change

**Problem ID: JSP-000925.**

We submit our **strict gap formalization, derivative-root selector existence and uniqueness theorem, and reproducible verification package** for JSP-000925 / Erdős Problem 1114.

This revision updates the existing PR #342. We propose changing the catalog's Lean-proof status from **No** to **Pending verification**, with proof references and attribution evidence. The current diff changes only the relevant catalog's **Lean proof** and **Attribution basis** fields. The proof, build files and verification materials are hosted in our proof repository.

## Our formalization contributions

1. We prove strict phase convexity and turn the credited non-strict analytic argument into strict outward gap comparisons.
2. We handle the central comparison when the number of derivative roots is even (the original polynomial has odd degree) and preserve the equality of the central mirror pair when symmetry requires it.
3. We construct a derivative zero in every interval between consecutive polynomial roots using Rolle's theorem.
4. We prove interval uniqueness through strict decrease of the logarithmic derivative and combine the construction with the strict gap theorem.
5. We supply a checksum-verified upstream bootstrap, locked dependencies, exact theorem audits, kernel replay, a negative control and NaNoda verification.

## Complete theorem scope

For an arbitrary nonzero real polynomial f of degree N+1, with N > 0 and roots a+d*j for j=0,...,N and d > 0, the complete endpoint constructs the unique derivative root b_k in each open interval between adjacent roots and proves reflection symmetry together with

```text
i+2 < N and N <= 2*(i+1) imply
b_(i+1) - b_i < b_(i+2) - b_(i+1).
```

Reflection gives the corresponding left-side monotonicity. The equal central mirror pair is excluded from strict comparisons. Translation, spacing, nonzero leading coefficient and degree are arbitrary. The cases N=1 and N=2 retain existence and uniqueness with no gap comparison required; a linear polynomial has no derivative-root gaps to compare. The complete endpoint does **not** assume a derivative-root selector or add unproved analytic hypotheses.

## Formal statement

- Mathematical review and candidate registration: Mathematical review must pass before Lean acceptance. Solver registration or an award claim by the mathematical solver is not a prerequisite for Lean verification or Lean candidate registration. The two contribution types can be registered independently.

- Original problem source and exact location: [Erdős Problem 1114](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1114), the derivative-root gap monotonicity question; independently checked against [Lorch (1976), printed page 293](https://real-j.mtak.hu/7424/1/MTA_ActaMathHung_27.pdf), whose introduction states the Erdos-Balint result. Direct access to erdosproblems.com was blocked during this review. The exact degree/root indexing and central equality case are set out in the pinned STATEMENT.md below.
- Current entry: [JSP-000925](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/main/problems/catalog-0901-1000.md#JSP-000925).
- Related Award claim: [#1585](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/issues/1585).
- Mathematical solution evidence to be reviewed first: The Bálint solution and cited Lorch literature are credited in the existing attribution and provenance record. The submitted source combines the attributed upstream analytic argument with the strictness, Rolle-existence and uniqueness proofs described below. These materials are submitted for mathematical review first; no existing organizer approval is asserted.
- Statement origin: **submitter-proposed statement requiring review**. No maintainer-approved challenge is asserted.
- Fixed statement and complete proof entry: [JSP000925Strict.lean](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7/projects/jsp-000925-strict/JSP000925Strict.lean), at `7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7`.
- Fully qualified target theorem(s): `JSP000925Strict.exists_unique_strict_gaps`, `JSP000925Strict.strict_gap_theorem`.
- Correspondence to the original problem: For N>0, d>0, a real nonzero polynomial of degree N+1 vanishing at a+d*j for every j=0,…,N, the endpoint constructs the unique derivative zero in each intervening open interval. It proves reflection symmetry and the strict outward comparison for i+2<N and N≤2(i+1). Reflection supplies the left-hand comparison; the central mirror pair stays equal. Small degrees retain existence and uniqueness with vacuous gap comparisons. No derivative-root selector is assumed, and no sign restriction on the leading coefficient is added.
- Connection: the statement and proof are the same Lean declaration; the checked audit imports the complete development rather than assuming a placeholder target.

## Reproduction

Prerequisites: Git, Bash, Python 3, elan and network access for pinned dependencies; Rust/Cargo is required for the existing NaNoda script. Use a separate full-history checkout for each selected proof version. Do not run `lake update`.

### Selected proof version 1

- Lean: `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0`, pinned in [lean-toolchain](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7/projects/jsp-000925-strict/lean-toolchain).
- Mathlib: `5ed2965256430c3649e86755f9576b54eca72435`; all nine dependency revisions are pinned in [lake-manifest.json](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7/projects/jsp-000925-strict/lake-manifest.json).
- Build instructions at the proof commit: [README.md](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7/projects/jsp-000925-strict/README.md). Later evidence-only documentation is linked separately below.

```bash
git clone --branch jsp-000925-strict-gaps https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean.git jsp-925-review-1
cd jsp-925-review-1
git checkout --detach 7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7
cd projects/jsp-000925-strict
elan toolchain install "$(cat lean-toolchain)"
python3 scripts/bootstrap.py
lake exe cache get
bash scripts/verify.sh
lake env lean Audit.lean
bash scripts/verify_nanoda.sh
```

[The audit entry](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7/projects/jsp-000925-strict/Audit.lean) contains `#print axioms` for the targets. Fresh verification on 2026-09-19 reproduced the following complete target axiom dependencies at the exact proof commit; the pinned report below covers every target and audit bridge:

```text
'JSP000925Strict.exists_unique_strict_gaps' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
'JSP000925Strict.strict_gap_theorem' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
```

Older runs in the historical sections below are retained as provenance. The completed supplemental workflow is documented separately below and is the basis of this updated self-check declaration. No independent human verifier is claimed.

## Proof submission

```json
[
  {
    "repository": "https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean",
    "branch": "jsp-000925-strict-gaps",
    "commit": "7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7"
  }
]
```

- **Exact theorem and file:** `JSP000925Strict.exists_unique_strict_gaps`; `JSP000925Strict.strict_gap_theorem` is the supporting strictness endpoint in [JSP000925Strict.lean](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7/projects/jsp-000925-strict/JSP000925Strict.lean).
- **Scope, contribution and build instructions:** [README.md](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/491ddda5bbaab48b4c2f4c5bff6b3b1f29ea1a58/projects/jsp-000925-strict/README.md).
- **Account-linked contribution and dependency attribution:** [PROVENANCE.md](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/491ddda5bbaab48b4c2f4c5bff6b3b1f29ea1a58/projects/jsp-000925-strict/PROVENANCE.md).
- **Executed verification receipt:** [VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/491ddda5bbaab48b4c2f4c5bff6b3b1f29ea1a58/projects/jsp-000925-strict/VERIFICATION.md).
- **Statement correspondence:** [STATEMENT.md](https://github.com/ketianzhang1-lang/jsp-000301-lean/blob/7b545f0e021b06d434654b17881c11819f3ff1b7/projects/jsp-000925-strict/STATEMENT.md).

The proof commit above is contained in the named branch. The README, provenance and receipt links identify a later documentation-only revision; the checked Lean source, dependency pins and verification scripts remain unchanged.

## Attribution and requested credit

Our contribution is recorded under GitHub account `ketianzhang1-lang`, with OpenAI ChatGPT assistance, for strict convexity, strict gap comparisons, the central-case argument, selector existence, interval uniqueness and verification. Mathematical credit remains

title: records(problems): record a Lean 4 formalization for JSP-000868
body:
## Submission type

- [ ] Mathematical solver information
- [x] Lean proof or formalization author information

## Problem and proposed change

Problem ID(s): JSP-000868

**Current entry.** `Lean proof` is `No`, `Current status` is `Solved`.

**Proposed change.** Record a complete Lean 4 formalization of the stated problem: set `Lean proof` to `Yes — [Lean source](https://github.com/Drag0ndddd1118/jsp-000868-formalization/blob/e39f14757e1f8ca21b91ec310047c10a56d73a36/Submission.lean)` in `problems/catalog-0801-0900.md`, add the matching `Attribution basis` row (`Lean: repository-owner attribution`, pointing at `README.md` and `Challenge.lean` of the same commit), and flip the corresponding row of `problems/README.md`.

- Mathematical solver: unchanged from the current entry (Erdős–Herzog–Piranian 1958, Pommerenke 1959); this PR claims no solver credit.
- Lean formalization author: GitHub account `Drag0ndddd1118` (Qin Zhao), who owns the linked repository and built and verified the development with Lean 4 and Mathlib. The proof script was drafted with AI assistance; the account holder is responsible for its content and performed the build and the axiom check. No individual AI model is listed as a contributor, in line with the catalog's attribution conventions.
- Independent verification: none claimed.

No other field is changed.

## Proof source

```json
[
  {
    "repository": "https://github.com/Drag0ndddd1118/jsp-000868-formalization",
    "branch": "main",
    "commit": "e39f14757e1f8ca21b91ec310047c10a56d73a36"
  }
]
```

**Repository layout.** `Challenge.lean` is the statement of record — it imports Mathlib and declares the proposition, proving nothing. `Submission.lean` imports it and proves the *same* constant. `check.py` type-checks the bridge between them and re-runs the axiom audit; CI runs `lake build` and that audit. The toolchain is `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0` and Mathlib is pinned to `5ed2965256430c3649e86755f9576b54eca72435` in `lake-manifest.json`.

**Statement of record** — `jsp000868Statement` in `Challenge.lean`:

```lean
def jsp000868Statement : Prop :=
  ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.eval 0 = 0 ∧
  IsConnected {z : ℂ | ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1} ∧
  ∃ z : ℂ, ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ 2 < ‖z‖
```

**Theorem proving it** — `JSP000868.jsp_000868` in `Submission.lean`.

**Why this covers the full original statement.** The question asks whether a polynomial whose unit-modulus sublevel set is connected must have that set inside a disk of radius two. The statement of record is its negation, and the submission discharges it with the explicit polynomial `p(z) = z(z-1)(z-2)`: it satisfies `p 0 = 0`, its lemniscate `{z : ‖p z‖ ≤ 1}` is **connected**, and the point `z = 58/25` lies in that set (`p(58/25) = 15312/15625 ≤ 1`) while `‖58/25‖ = 2.32 > 2`. So the sublevel set is connected but is not contained in any disk of radius two centred at the origin.

Connectedness is not assumed: it is proved from scratch. Writing `z = x + iy`, `‖p(x+iy)‖² = (x²+y²)((x-1)²+y²)((x-2)²+y²)` is a polynomial in `y²` with positive coefficients, so each vertical fibre `{y | ‖p(x+iy)‖ ≤ 1}` is order-convex and contains `0` when nonempty; the real slice `{x | |p x| ≤ 1}` is order-convex as well (from `p(2-x) = -p(x)` and the critical values `±2/(3√3)`, whose modulus is below `1`); and the sublevel set is the union of those fibres over the real slice, every one of which meets the common point `0`.

**Completeness.** `Submission.lean` contains no `axiom`, no `opaque`, no `sorry`, no `admit`, no `unsafe` and no `native_decide`. `check.py` type-checks the bridge `example : jsp000868Statement := JSP000868.jsp_000868` — which can only succeed if the submission proves exactly the proposition that `Challenge.lean` states — and audits `#print axioms JSP000868.jsp_000868`, which reports `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. Both CI steps are part of the repository.

## Submission checklist

- [x] I changed only solver attribution, Lean proof information or supporting sources in the relevant catalog.
- [x] I supplied the evidence required for the type of change above.
- [x] The mathematical result fully solves the original problem. Any submitted Lean proof is complete at the specified commit, with no `sorry`, `admit` or added unproved assumptions in the proof of that result.
- [x] This PR contains no proof source files, archives, binaries or vendored dependencies.
- [x] Any Lean reference identifies a commit contained in the named branch and the exact version for review.

title: JSP-000937: catalog Lean evidence and formalization attribution
body:
## Submission type

- [ ] Mathematical solver information
- [x] Lean proof or formalization author information

## Problem

- Problem ID: **JSP-000937**; original source: [Erdős problem 1130](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1130).
- Mathematical solution/review reference: The all-gap maximin interpolation problem, associated with de Boor and Pinkus (1978), plus the logarithmic request on the original Erdős 1130 page. Mathematical and formal-statement correspondence remain for maintainer review.
- Current catalog entry says `Lean proof: No`; this PR changes only this problem's `Lean proof` and `Attribution basis` rows to a scoped external proof reference. It leaves solver status, eligibility, and other records unchanged.
- Companion claim/evidence: [#152](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/issues/152). This reuses the existing single-problem PR #765 after #144 was closed; it is not a new priority date.
- Priority/related work: Related #1566 cites our original repository and exact old SHA while disclaiming proof authorship; it is a catalog registration, not an independent competing proof. #1680 addresses a stronger all-peaks-equal statement and #2036 describes partial numerical scope. Please compare any independently earlier complete Target937 proof before assigning priority; we do not assert global firstness from the absence of one in this bounded comparison.

## Formal statement

- [Independent proposed statement](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a/Erdos1153/JSPInterpolation/Definitions.lean); it has not been approved as an official benchmark statement.
- Exact target: `JSPFreeNodes.jsp_000937 : JSPFreeNodes.Target937`.
- Correspondence: Target937 is the conjunction of (i) existence and classification of maximizers of the minimum of all n+1 interval peaks, including both exterior intervals and the one-node case, and (ii) a single C>0 with allMinPeak(X)≤C log n for every n≥2 and every node family. The reference shape is normalized, but competitors are free-node; the exterior peaks are required to be at least the reference height, not all equal. The clause-by-clause mapping is in [STATEMENT-CORRESPONDENCE.md](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a/STATEMENT-CORRESPONDENCE.md).
- Low-cardinality check: for two nodes every placement has all-gap minimum `1`; the pair `(-1/2, 1/2)` has exterior peaks `2` and internal peak `1`. The literal maximization therefore cannot require all peaks to be equal in this case; see the [calculation](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/4d7493e7e730597877c38bd750bf02839863b68a/verification/2026-09-23-fro/LOW_N_SCOPE.md).

## Proof submission

```json
[
  {
    "repository": "https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean",
    "branch": "main",
    "commit": "c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a"
  }
]
```

- [Proof file](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a/Erdos1153/JSPInterpolation/Logarithmic.lean) and target above. The final theorem is the conjunction of jsp_000937_classification and jsp_000937_logarithmic; Audit937.lean checks the full target type, and AuditFull.lean checks the related entries and axioms.
- Historical public proof snapshot: [`9f249379d6d96e9e70f91e2c22982f96a23de2da`](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/tree/9f249379d6d96e9e70f91e2c22982f96a23de2da) with [submitter CI run 35125716929](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/actions/runs/35125716929). Its 4.27.0 checks establish historical publication evidence, not verification of the new commit.

## Reproduction

- `lean-toolchain`: [Lean 4.33.0](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a/lean-toolchain); pinned Mathlib `db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d` in [lakefile.toml](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a/lakefile.toml) and [lake-manifest.json](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a/lake-manifest.json).
- From a clean checkout of the exact commit: `bash verify.sh`. The script builds the target, checks its declaration and statement bridge, reports transitive axioms, scans trust-sensitive source, and runs `leanchecker`.
- Direct target build: `lake build Erdos1153.JSPInterpolation.Logarithmic`. Axiom audit: `lake env lean AuditFull.lean`. Kernel replay: `lake env leanchecker Erdos1153.JSPInterpolation.Logarithmic`.
- The selected target's `#print axioms` output is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. [Local command/results record](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a/evidence/lean433-local-verification.md); [Linux CI run 35849587676](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/actions/runs/35849587676). These are submitter-run checks, not organizer verification. A [separate FRO comparator self-check](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/4d7493e7e730597877c38bd750bf02839863b68a/verification/2026-09-23-fro/README.md) used the Lean 4.33.0-compatible comparator and Landrun in a network-disconnected Linux container. Both the Lean default kernel and the nanoda external kernel accepted the selected proof with only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The challenge imports the submitted definition layer, so independent problem-to-statement review remains necessary. The evidence-only follow-up commit is `4d7493e7e730597877c38bd750bf02839863b68a`; the proof submission remains `c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a`.

## Attribution

- Mathematical solver(s): the historical publication authors cited above; this PR does not seek solver credit.
- Lean contribution claimed: `randyxian08`, with inherited work and AI assistance disclosed in the pinned source. The submitting account owns the original proof repository. PROVENANCE.md distinguishes the credited `ethn-y/erdos-1153-lean` base and AI assistance from the submitted all-gap and logarithmic extension. Repository control supports traceability but does not by itself settle independent identity verification.
- Independent verifier: none named. Identity, statement coverage, priority, and award eligibility remain for the organizers to determine.

## Submission checklist

- [x] Only the relevant catalog entry's permitted Lean proof and attribution text changes; the PR adds no Lean source or private contact data.
- [x] The selected proof is submitted as a complete answer to the original problem, with no `sorry`, `admit`, or added unproved mathematical assumptions in the checked target; statement correspondence remains subject to review.
- [x] The proof is from the submitting account's original repository, pinned to a 40-character SHA on `main`, with reproduction and axiom evidence above.


## Dated original-task verification supplement — 2026-11-09

[Complete review, formula bridges, pinned inputs, raw checks and resource/retry evidence](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/99808b41a3cc5e77ab2abec6a1632c1fea3c9e2d/verification/2026-11-09-review/report.md) are public at evidence-only commit `99808b41a3cc5e77ab2abec6a1632c1fea3c9e2d`. The selected proof remains `c6819617f4d8de6afcbf63da31544ce2902f7b6a`; all 86 original tracked Lean files and pins were unchanged during this review.

The unmodified Lean 4.33.0 project build, 8 explicit theorem/bridge source and axiom checks, both original audit files and a low-memory Lean kernel replay passed. The default parallel replay was first killed by OOM (exit 137); retrying with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1` passed without modifying the proof or weakening the checker. Each audited declaration has only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

Semantic review covers both literal main real-interval requests: the maximizer classification over unrestricted distinct nodes, all n+1 intervals including the exterior two, and a single uniform positive logarithmic constant for n≥2, with one-node classification separate. The [mathematical discussion](https://github.com/randyxian08/jsp000937-lean/blob/99808b41a3cc5e77ab2abec6a1632c1fea3c9e2d/verification/2026-11-09-review/math-review.md) explicitly distinguishes the original paper's fixed-endpoint internal-peak theorem from the all-gap problem and explains the two-node counterexample to the webpage background's stronger all-peaks-equal necessity. That stronger assertion is not claimed.

This is AI-assisted submitter-side review, not independent human or organizer verification. No fresh FRO/nanoda run, identity confirmation, first-formalization priority or award acceptance is inferred. Claim #152 still has no merged-contribution prerequisite; this supplement requests proof/scope review in the existing PR and does not create a new claim or priority timestamp.

title: Formalize JSP-000937 (Erdős Problem #1129 / #1130 · Optimal Peak Lebesgue Interpolation Nodes)
body:
### Summary

This PR updates the catalog for JSP-000937 (Erdős Problem #1129 / #1130: Which interpolation nodes maximize the smallest peak error-amplification factor among intervals between consecutive nodes?) to indicate that a formal proof in Lean 4 has been completed.

- Standalone formalization & DefEq bridge repository: https://github.com/Drag0ndddd1118/jsp-000937-formalization
- Mathematical resolution: Resolved by Carl de Boor and Allan Pinkus (1978), proving that equioscillation does not characterize all global maximizers of the minimum gap peak of the Lebesgue function by exhibiting a three-node maximizer without equal gap peaks.
- Axioms: Standard Lean foundation `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` (0 custom axioms, 0 sorry, 0 admit)
- Verification: Complete GitHub Actions CI green & automated double-checked with `check.py`

Links to prior catalog submissions: none

title: Record the Lean formalization of JSP-000930
body:
## Submission type

- [x] Lean proof or formalization author information

## Problem

- **Problem** JSP-000930 / Erdős Problem 1119, originally Hayman's Problem 2.46. [Original statement](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1119)
- **Catalog change** Record a Lean formalization of ZFC independence and link the published negative consistency result. [Current entry](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/main/problems/catalog-0901-1000.md#JSP-000930)
- **Related submissions** PRs #1403 and #5278 cite the Lean formalization of the countable Wetzel case and the positive implication with the hypothesis `m⁺ < 𝔠`. PR #179 formalizes the historical countable case. This submission proves independence for the original quantified statement, including opposite answers for `m = ℵ₁` in two models with `𝔠 = ℵ₂`. [#1403](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/pull/1403) · [#5278](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/pull/5278) · [#179](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/pull/179) · [Existing Lean formalization](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1119.lean)

## Formal statement

- **Complete mathematical solution** Ashutosh Kumar and Saharon Shelah, *On a question about families of entire functions*, Fund. Math. **239** (2017), 279–288, Theorem 2.1, establish the positive consistency direction. Jonathan Schilhan and Thilo Weinert, *Wetzel families and the continuum*, J. Lond. Math. Soc. **109** (2024), e12918, §5, establish the negative consistency direction. [Kumar–Shelah](https://doi.org/10.4064/fm252-3-2017) · [Schilhan–Weinert §5](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.19473v3#S5)
- **Review and statement origin** The catalog review records independence from ZFC. The formal sentence follows Hayman's Problem 2.46 and is provided for statement review. [Catalog review](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/main/problems/catalog-0901-1000.md#JSP-000930)
- **Target** `JSP000930.Consistency.hayman_1119_relative_independence`. [Pinned statement](https://github.com/meowmath-ai/MeowLean/blob/a25145bf1c579e654d377e8930679de576357584/supplements/JSP-000930/src/JSP000930RelativeIndependence.lean#L35)
- **Correspondence** The sentence quantifies over ordinal representatives of bounds strictly between ℵ₀ and 𝔠. At each complex point it bounds the exact evaluation image of a family of entire functions and concludes the same bound for the family. Entire Taylor codes have infinite radius of convergence. The evaluation relation agrees with the Taylor limit. The two models satisfy ZFC and `𝔠 = ℵ₂`, with opposite truth values for that same sentence. [Statement and proof correspondence](https://github.com/meowmath-ai/MeowLean/blob/a25145bf1c579e654d377e8930679de576357584/solutions/JSP-000930.md)
